title: Orchard AI inference economics snapshot (Jul 2025) - draft
content:
Executive summary:
Orchard AI is running a multimodal chatbot workload with an average of 45M input tokens and 90M output tokens per month. This draft quantifies a set of Redwood Optimize recommendations (model variant selection, int8 quantization, prefix/KV caching, and dynamic batching tweaks) and shows an expected 38–45% reduction in monthly inference spend under our baseline traffic profile.

Key takeaways:
- Baseline monthly spend (observed): $134,200
- Modeled post-Optimize spend (recommended stack): $82,700 (approx. 38% savings)
- Biggest drivers: quantization + model downgrades (25–30% of savings), batching/cache improvements (8–12% of savings), minor infra tuning and routing (3–5%).
- Risk buckets: quality drift (must monitor eval set), cache-hit variance, model compatibility for int8 kernels.

Assumptions used in model (explicit):
- Traffic profile: 1.5M queries/month, average prompt length 30 tokens, average completion 60 tokens -> 135 tokens/query avg.
- Token mix: 25% long-form (>=512 tokens), 75% short (<512 tokens).
- Hardware pricing: A100 (40GB) spot-equivalent cost modeled at $3.60/hr GPU-hour, H100 at $8.20/hr (on-prem equivalent cost used where applicable).
- Baseline model: vXX-lm-13b-fp16 (serving kernel FP16).
- Recommended model variants: vXX-lm-13b-int8 / vXX-lm-7b-int8 for tail routing (compatible with Redwood runtime int8 kernels).
- Average throughput per A100: baseline 120 tokens/s; int8 variant 180 tokens/s (due to lower memory/compute).
- Cache & batching: expected steady-state prefix KV cache hit 18% (conservative), dynamic batching improvement adds another 12% effective throughput at p95.

Before / After snapshot (monthly):
(rounded numbers for executive view)

| Component                 | Baseline ($) | Post-Optimize ($) | Delta ($) | Notes                             |
|--------------------------|--------------:|-------------------:|----------:|-----------------------------------|
| GPU compute (primary)    |      96,400   |          61,300    |  35,100   | Model quant + int8 gains + batching|
| Overflow routing (H100)  |       9,600   |           6,200    |   3,400   | fewer fallbacks after routing fix |
| Storage / artifacts      |       2,100   |           1,900    |     200   | minor snapshot consolidation      |
| Egress / networking      |       4,200   |           3,700    |     500   | cache reduces repeated outputs    |
| Redwood platform fees    |      12,900   |           9,200    |   3,700   | tier change + reserved bursts     |
| SRE/ops buffer (conting.)|       8,000   |           0 (inc)  |   8,000   | absorbed into platform fee model  |
| TOTAL                   |     134,200   |          82,700    |  51,500   | ~38% savings                       |

Notes on calculations and thought process:
- GPU compute is modeled via token-seconds converted to GPU-hours using measured throughput from Redwood perf bench for Orchard-specific prompts (sampled week of 2025-06-20). Baseline throughput (fp16) = 120 tok/s/A100; int8 variant = 180 tok/s/A100.
- We assume a conservative int8 model accuracy delta: 0.6% drop on Orchard's core intent-recognition eval set; tradeoff acceptable for 13B -> int8 gains. Team should validate with the 1,500 example prompt set before rollout.
- Batching policy adjustments (max_batch_size increase, lower batch-timeout at p95) recovers ~12% throughput at cost of small p99 latency tail increases; we recommend p95-targeted rollout only for non-interactive routes.
- Prefix/KV cache: estimated 18% hit rate based on Orchard's repeated-system message and templated prompts. If hit rate reaches 30%, additional 6–8% savings observed.

Micro-scenarios (sensitivity):
1) Cache-hit low case (10%): Post-opt spend -> $89.3k (33% savings)
2) Cache-hit mid (18%, base case): $82.7k (38% savings)
3) High cache (30%): $76.1k (43% savings)
4) Quality-trigger (int8 accuracy regression >1.5%): revert model downgrade for 30% of traffic -> blended savings drop to ~22%

Actionable recommendations (short list):
1) Run an int8 A/B on 10% of traffic for 2 weeks using Orchard's 1.5k eval prompts + live shadow monitoring (metrics: intent-F1, hallucination rate, user satisfaction proxy).
2) Enable prefix/KV cache for templated routes and deploy cache TTL of 30s for dynamic contexts; measure hit-rate after 72 hours and iterate.
3) Update batching policy on dedicated routes: increase max_batch_size by 1.6x, reduce batch timeout to 12ms for user-facing priority routes, and keep a canary route for p99 latency.
4) Reserve small dedicated capacity (1 A100-equivalent pool) for canary/rollback to avoid H100 spot volatility.
5) Create automated regression alerting (Redwood Console) for the Orchard eval set; set action to rollback model variant if intent-F1 drops >1.0% over 24h.

Operational rollout plan (30-day):
Week 1: Prep A/B pipelines, calibrate int8 kernels on sample checkpoint, baseline evals.
Week 2: Start 10% int8 A/B + cache enabled for templated routes, collect metrics.
Week 3: Expand to 30% if metrics stable, apply batching policy updates for non-interactive traffic.
Week 4: Full rollout with reserved capacity and cost monitoring dashboards; finalize committed capacity if observed savings align to projection.

Open questions / risks to resolve before full commit:
- Confirm int8 kernel parity on Orchard's longest-context prompts (>=2k tokens); some int8 kernels may require fallback for very long sequences.
- Legal / compliance check for storing prompt prefixes in cache (PII risk).
- Align on acceptable latency p99 delta for interactive product owners (product wants <=1.2x baseline).

Appendix: compact calc example (how we got GPU compute):
- Monthly token volume = 135 tokens/q * 1.5M q = 202.5M tokens/month.
- Baseline compute seconds = tokens / (tok/sec) -> for fp16: 202.5M / 120 = 1,687,500 s = 468.75 GPU-hours/month per A100-equivalent workload unit.
- Cost baseline (compute) ~ 468.75 * $3.60/hr * active_pools_factor (x55 units across day) -> numbers adjusted to match observed telemetry. (we include full calc sheet in linked Confluence).

Next deliverables (by 2025-07-28):
- Detailed spreadsheet (sheet id: CONFLUENCE-REDWOOD-5872/sheet-2) with per-route line items and per-model perf traces.
- Short runbook for rollback criteria and alert thresholds.
- Finalized recommended committed capacity proposal (if Orchard wants >30% savings locked in, we need a 12-mo reserved capacity quote).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally conservative on cache-hit and int8 accuracy to avoid overstating savings. Numbers should be used for initial sales + solutions-eng conversations, not as a signed contract.
- Comments inline welcome: I left a few "TODO" markers in the sheet for Orchard-specific route names and exact traffic splits.

Prepared by: Marissa (product-optimize)
Reviewers: Ethan P., Lina K., Rahul M.
